tables.html:
Investment riskThe present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated using a discount rate determined by reference to high quality corporate bond yields; if the actual return on plan assets is below the assumed rate, it will create a plan deficit. Currently, the defined benefit plan has a relatively balanced investment in equity securities and debt instruments. Due to the long-term nature of the defined benefit plan obligation, the pension committee considers it appropriate that a reasonable portion of the plan assets should be invested in equity instruments to leverage the return generated by the fund.
Interest riskA decrease in the bond interest rate will increase the defined benefit plan obligation, particularly on a solvency basis. Although this will be partially offset by an increase in the return of the defined benefit plan's investments, the impact may be material as pension liabilities are sensitive to variations in interest rates.
Longevity riskThe present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated based on assumptions regarding mortality rates of plan participants both during and after their employment. An increase in the life expectancy of the plan participants will increase the defined benefit obligation.
Inflation riskThe present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated by reference to the inflation rate. As such, a higher inflation rate than projected will increase the defined benefit plan's liability.

information_blocks.information_block: Investment risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated using a discount rate determined by reference to high quality corporate bond yields; if the actual return on plan assets is below the assumed rate, it will create a plan deficit. Currently, the defined benefit plan has a relatively balanced investment in equity securities and debt instruments. Due to the long-term nature of the defined benefit plan obligation, the pension committee considers it appropriate that a reasonable portion of the plan assets should be invested in equity instruments to leverage the return generated by the fund. This information is part of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for Yellow Pages Limited as of December 31, 2022, with all amounts presented in thousands of Canadian dollars.

Interest risk: A decrease in the bond interest rate will increase the defined benefit plan obligation, particularly on a solvency basis. Although this will be partially offset by an increase in the return of the defined benefit plan's investments, the impact may be material as pension liabilities are sensitive to variations in interest rates. This information is part of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for Yellow Pages Limited as of December 31, 2022, with all amounts presented in thousands of Canadian dollars.

Longevity risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated based on assumptions regarding mortality rates of plan participants both during and after their employment. An increase in the life expectancy of the plan participants will increase the defined benefit obligation. This information is part of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for Yellow Pages Limited as of December 31, 2022, with all amounts presented in thousands of Canadian dollars.

Inflation risk: The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated by reference to the inflation rate. As such, a higher inflation rate than projected will increase the defined benefit's liability. This information is part of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for Yellow Pages Limited as of December 31, 2022, with all amounts presented in thousands of Canadian dollars.

table_cells.text: The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated using a discount rate determined by reference to high quality corporate bond  yields; if the actual return on plan assets is below the assumed rate, it will create a plan deficit. Currently, the defined benefit plan has a relatively  balanced investment in equity securities and debt instruments. Due to the long-term nature of the defined benefit plan obligation, the pension  committee considers it appropriate that a reasonable portion of the plan assets should be invested in equity instruments to leverage the return  generated by the fund.

A decrease in the bond interest rate will increase the defined benefit plan obligation, particularly on a solvency basis.  Although this will be partially  offset by an increase in the return of the defined benefit plan's investments, the impact may be material as pension liabilities are sensitive to variations  in interest rates.

The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated based on assumptions regarding mortality rates of plan participants both during  and after their employment. An increase in the life expectancy of the plan participants will increase the defined benefit obligation.

The present value of the defined benefit plan obligation is calculated by reference to the inflation rate. As such, a higher inflation rate than projected  will increase the defined benefit plan's liability.

The categories include Canadian pooled equity funds, global pooled equity funds, emerging markets pooled equity funds, Canadian pooled fixed-income funds, pooled real estate funds, pooled private equity funds, pooled infrastructure funds, and cash and cash equivalents. The values for 2022 and 2021 are as follows: Canadian pooled equity funds (4.5% in 2022, 4.5% in 2021), global pooled equity funds (23.5% in 2022, 25.0% in 2021), emerging markets pooled equity funds (9.5% in 2022, 10.0% in 2021), Canadian pooled fixed-income funds (36.0% in 2022, 44.0% in 2021), pooled real estate funds (14.0% in 2022, 10.5% in 2021), pooled private equity funds (6.0% in 2022, 4.0% in 2021), pooled infrastructure funds (4.5% in 2022, 2.0% in 2021), and cash and cash equivalents (2.0% in 2022, 0.0% in 2021). The data is sourced from the Yellow Pages Limited Annual Report 2022.

Pooled fund units are part of the fair value of the plan assets as at December 31, 2022 and 2021. The table categorizes these units into various types, including Canadian pooled equity funds, global pooled equity funds, emerging markets pooled equity funds, Canadian pooled fixed-income funds, pooled real estate funds, pooled private equity funds, pooled infrastructure funds, and cash and cash equivalents. The values for these categories are expressed in percentages for the years 2022 and 2021.

Pooled real estate funds accounted for 14.0% of the fair value of the plan assets as at December 31, 2022, an increase from 10.5% in 2021. This category is included in the pooled fund units.
Pooled private equity funds represented 6.0% of the fair value of the plan assets as at December 31, 2022, up from 4.0% in 2021. This category is part of the pooled fund units.
